title: JANUS Linear A SigLA structural schema interpretation after frozen three-page probe

observed_boundary.reason: The only three-way common paths are page/image scaffolding. The frozen sample does not support promoting a repeated descendant path to a universal content-unit extraction grammar.

important_heterogeneity.reason: A class label present in one document can motivate a separately predeclared capability audit, but cannot retroactively redefine the frozen three-page common-path gate.

methodological_connections.name: INTERFACE_CONTRACT_GENERALITY_AND_CONTENT_SCHEMA_GENERALITY_ARE_SEPARATE_GATES
methodological_connections.statement: The same word-view interface can validate across heterogeneous documents while content-bearing descendant structures vary enough that no universal extraction unit is established by the initial interface sample.

methodological_connections.name: A_SOURCE_NATIVE_SEMANTIC_CLASS_LABEL_IS_NOT_AUTOMATICALLY_A_UNIVERSAL_SCHEMA
methodological_connections.statement: The DOM class token 'word' is technically observable and source-native, but its presence in selected pages must be inventoried independently before it can become a frozen extraction rule.

methodological_connections.name: NEGATIVE_SCHEMA_RESULT_SHOULD_CHANGE_SAMPLING_QUESTION_NOT_RELAX_THE_GATE
methodological_connections.statement: After a heterogeneous frozen sample yields no common content-unit path, the next experiment should measure structural capability prevalence on a predeclared sample rather than weaken the original commonality criterion.

next_gate.goal: Select a new deterministic hash sample from the already frozen 686-pair identity bridge before live content fetch, validate the frozen SigLA adapter contract per page, and inventory source-native DOM structural families without reading mwenge transcription content or using literal SigLA text for selection.
